repo.name: bookem-user
repo.description: User portal for Book'em's volunteer management system.
repo.customer: Book'em staff and volunteers coordinating literacy programs.
repo.sourceNote: Seeded demo data modeled after the public repository structure and nonprofit volunteer-management domain.

prs.title: Fix volunteer signup session loss after invite redirect
prs.author: sam
businessTrace: Touches volunteer registration, the front door for new Book'em volunteers.
Linked to support notes about invited users abandoning signup after redirect.
Adds regression coverage around the exact invite/session failure.
observabilitySignals: Support complaints about invite redirects fell from 7/week to 1/week

agentFindings.finding: Signup failure blocks volunteer activation, directly harming program capacity.
Strong evidence: linked support complaints, auth path diff, regression test.
Small session helper cleanup reduces future auth fragility.
Low activity footprint with clear outcome; not inflated.

prs.rankReason: Small diff protects the volunteer onboarding funnel, which is business-critical for the nonprofit.

prs.title: Remove dead availability branches from booking request flow
prs.author: zine
prs.verdict: Maintenance work that protects a valuable workflow.
businessTrace: Removes unused branching in the booking flow used by volunteers requesting sessions.
Keeps the scheduling path easier to reason about before peak volunteer season.
Adds tests proving no regression in booking request eligibility.
observabilitySignals: Median time to submit booking request improved from 2m 14s to 1m 39s

agentFindings.finding: Simplifies active code in a mission-critical path; this is not janitorial churn.
Users may not see a new feature, but they benefit through fewer booking failures.
Test coverage helps, but production booking-failure telemetry is missing.
Net code removal plus targeted tests is a strong anti-Goodhart signal.

prs.rankReason: Protects the reliability and maintainability of an active workflow that users depend on.

prs.title: Add Cypress coverage for volunteer onboarding happy path
prs.author: maya
prs.verdict: High leverage because it guards the most important user journey.
businessTrace: Covers account creation, profile completion, and first booking request.
Runs in CI, preventing regressions before volunteers hit them.
Targets the path most closely tied to volunteer activation.
observabilitySignals: 2 onboarding regressions caught in CI before production
Main branch onboarding failure rate stayed at 0% during next 5 merges

agentFindings.finding: Indirect impact, but on a critical journey.
Executable proof exists in CI.
Future PRs become safer and cheaper to review.
Test code can be gamed, but this targets a real workflow.

prs.rankReason: Does not ship visible UI, but materially lowers risk around volunteer activation.

prs.title: Speed up volunteer dashboard by memoizing assignment cards
prs.author: rachel
prs.verdict: Likely useful, but needs real latency telemetry.
businessTrace: Touches the dashboard volunteers use to see assignments.
Reduces repeated card rendering when filters change.
No real user performance measurement is attached.

agentFindings.finding: Dashboard responsiveness affects repeat volunteer usage.
No before/after Web Vitals or interaction timing.
Memoization is contained and readable.
Performance claims without measurements are easy to overstate.

prs.rankReason: Promising user impact, but the product needs instrumentation before calling it proven.

prs.title: Clarify empty states for users with no active assignments
prs.author: ana
prs.verdict: Useful UX polish with moderate impact evidence.
businessTrace: Targets a confusing first-session state for newly approved volunteers.
May reduce support questions about whether signup worked.
No support-ticket link or activation metric is attached.

agentFindings.finding: Improves user confidence during onboarding.
Impact hypothesis is plausible but under-evidenced.
Small isolated UI component.
Small honest UX change; not inflated.

prs.rankReason: Likely helps confused users, but impact is softer than signup or booking reliability.

prs.title: Upgrade Next.js and patch transitive dependencies
prs.author: devin
prs.verdict: Legitimate maintenance, but activity metrics overstate the work.
businessTrace: Patches framework dependencies and reduces security/runtime risk.
Most line changes are lockfile churn.
No user-facing behavior change expected.

agentFindings.finding: Keeping the platform current matters, especially for a volunteer portal.
Dependency audit passes, but no security advisory is linked.
Impact is risk reduction, not immediate UX.
Large line count is mostly generated lockfile diff; do not reward it as feature output.

prs.rankReason: Necessary maintenance, but not as impactful as PRs protecting volunteer activation.

prs.title: Reorganize dashboard styles and rename card variants
prs.author: lee
prs.verdict: Looks busy, weak business value evidence.
businessTrace: Mostly renames style variants and moves CSS blocks.
No issue, user complaint, accessibility bug, or design goal linked.
Touches many files without changing user-visible workflow outcomes.
observabilitySignals: No linked ticket, support issue, or design QA artifact
High file churn, low outcome evidence

agentFindings.finding: High commit count and file churn with weak outcome evidence.
No clear volunteer or staff benefit.
Could be useful if it reduces future UI duplication, but that claim is not proven.
Missing before/after screenshots, design issue, or test coverage.

prs.rankReason: Classic Goodhart risk: big visible diff, little evidence of business or maintenance impact.

prs.title: Add volunteer role badges to profile header
prs.author: nina
prs.verdict: Do not merge as 'impactful' until the intended outcome is explicit.
businessTrace: May help staff and volunteers understand permissions.
Could also be decorative if no confusion exists today.
Needs author response: what behavior should change?

agentFindings.finding: No business outcome stated by PR author.
Role visibility can reduce confusion if permissions are a real pain point.
Small UI addition could be honest or cosmetic; ask for evidence.

prs.rankReason: Open PR should trigger an impact-intent comment rather than a final ranking.

openPrComment.body:
Goodhart Police impact check:

This PR may be useful, but its business outcome is currently under-specified.

Please answer before merge:
1. What user or business outcome should improve if this ships?
2. Who benefits: volunteers, Book'em staff, coordinators, or maintainers?
3. How will we know it worked after merge?

Suggested measurement if you want the police to instrument this:
- profile_role_badge_viewed
- permission_confusion_support_ticket
- role_based_action_blocked

Current verdict: plausible impact, insufficient evidence.
